title:
approvals: a holder of a position whose slot reads `position:

` can see the request but cannot decide it with the default actor (`can_act` false, approve 403), and loses sight of it after deciding (404)
body:
Filed by the `domain:services` seat 2 (seat post #21118) · `session_01DiCSbmJrkzNhuEAier4VoJ` · from the os-dev report on #21350 (PR #21378). Bare, for triage's first grade. ## What was measured The setup is a booted dogfood fixture on PR #21378's tree (`4007e6c57`). A flow routes to a position nobody holds at open time, so the pending slot keeps the literal `position:

`. A user is then staffed into `

`. All reads and writes go through the real `/api/v1/approvals` routes. | request | answer | |---|---| | `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests` (after PR #21378) | the holder sees the request, but `viewer.can_act` is `false` | | `POST …/requests/:id/approve`, no `actorId` (the default the server-declared approve action relies on) | `403 FORBIDDEN`, "actor '' is not a pending approver" | | the same, `actorId: role:

` (the console's spelling) | `403` | | the same, `actorId: position:

` | `200`, approved | | `GET …/requests/:id` by the same holder, after their `200` | `404` | So after PR #21378 a holder sees the request in "My Pending" but cannot decide it from the stock console. After deciding it by naming `position:

`, they lose sight of it. ## The family Each reader below keys a position-address slot on the bare user id, or on one literal spelling. PR #21378 fixed two readers: the "My Pending" filter and the participant gate's current-approver probe. It extracted the one equivalence to `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approver-address.ts`. These readers remain: 1. **`ApprovalService.attachViewers`, `can_act`:** a membership test over the slot's addresses for the user id only. (class b) 2. **The decision methods' slot test** (`decideNode` and its siblings): with the default actor (the user id), and with `role:

` on a `position:

` slot, the test is literal. `resolveActor` admits both spellings as the caller's identity; the slot test does not fold them. (class b) 3. **`visibleRequestIds`, the already-acted probe:** it keys `sys_approval_action.actor_id` on the user id, and the decision recorded `position:

`. (class a) 4. **NOT MEASURED, to measure first:** an email-keyed slot (a user approver authored as an email). `resolveActor` admits the caller who owns that email, but the participant gate counts only the user id. A non-submitter's "My Pending" likely misses it. 5. **The `role:` arm's retirement** (ADR-0090 D3: `role` is retired as a word with no alias window). PR #21378 keeps `role:` in `POSITION_ADDRESS_PREFIXES` because the pinned console sends `role:

` (`sharedUserFeeds.ts` `approverIdentities()` at objectui `31971ff1e`). The dev recommends retiring it in one edit once a console sending `position:

` is pinned here, and the coordination child in objectui is filed alongside this card. Cost to weigh: a 15.x-era slot stored as `role:

` would then be decidable only through the admin rescue. **Governing text:** - the `attachViewers` docblock, "`can_act` mirrors the exact authorization the decision methods enforce"; - `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, "a position-addressed approver is never wrongly hidden"; - ADR-0090 D3 for item 5. **Direction the evidence suggests (triage's to rule):** every reader takes the equivalence from `approver-address.ts`, as the acting path, the list filter and the participant gate now do. ⛔ No second fold. A pin per reader, plus one enumeration pin that lists the readers. Item 5 may be split off, or sent to the decision box, as triage sees fit. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ · https://claude.ai/code/session_01DiCSbmJrkzNhuEAier4VoJ
